positioning: MSO is designed to be the most complete mobile-first, AI-native private Linux workspace for an owner or small trusted team. It does not claim to replace specialist products at their strongest specialty.

criteria.label: Browser workspace
criteria.definition: A unified browser workspace with mobile-aware navigation across files, terminal, editors, apps, and host views.

criteria.label: Linux host administration
criteria.definition: General Linux host operations such as services, logs, package visibility, network, storage, users, and system configuration.

criteria.label: Application delivery
criteria.definition: Application/container deployment, Git integration, previews, lifecycle, backups, and rollback.

criteria.label: Monitoring and observability
criteria.definition: Metrics, history, alerting, anomaly detection, correlations, and incident analysis.

criteria.label: Roles and delegation
criteria.definition: Least-privilege roles, multiple identities/devices, auditability, and SSO or policy integration.

criteria.label: Built-in AI and MCP
criteria.definition: Built-in AI assistance plus structured remote tool/API control of the workspace.

workspace.note: Files, real PTY, code/media editors, managed apps, responsive shells, PWA, and CLI share one API surface.

hostOps.note: Live metrics/processes, service inventory and logs, exact allowlisted systemd lifecycle, package-cache visibility, full owner shell. No first-class network/storage/user administration yet.

delivery.note: Pinned managed-app install/update/backup/rollback paths exist, but MSO is not yet a general Git-to-container PaaS.

observability.note: Live host metrics and processes are built in; long-term history, alert rules, anomaly correlation, and RCA remain specialist gaps.

delegation.note: Approved devices have live Viewer, Operator, and Owner roles with audit and immediate revocation. This is not a full user directory, Linux-account mapping, or SSO system.

aiControl.note: BYOK Alfa, structured host/editor tools, remote OAuth/PKCE MCP, CLI parity, and project-aware tool discovery are native product surfaces.

workspace.note: Integrated browser administration and terminal, with optional applications; not an editor-centric mobile workspace.

hostOps.note: Network, firewall, storage, logs, software updates, users, systemd, VMs, containers, and multi-server administration.

delivery.note: Can administer containers and VMs, but is not primarily a Git-to-production PaaS.

observability.note: Detailed host metrics and journal correlation, without Netdata-class alerting/anomaly depth.

delegation.note: Uses normal Linux users and privileges and supports network-wide login/SSO approaches.

aiControl.note: No built-in AI assistant or remote MCP control plane in the core product.

workspace.note: Dashboard and real-time terminal center on deployed resources rather than a general files/editors workspace.

hostOps.note: Server setup automations, terminal, monitoring, and cleanup; not a general Linux administration cockpit.

delivery.note: Git integrations, automatic and preview deployments, one-click services, SSL, databases, backups, webhooks, and API.

observability.note: Deployment/server/container monitoring and notifications, but not deep per-second anomaly/RCA analytics.

delegation.note: Team projects, roles, and permissions are first-class product features.

aiControl.note: No native AI workspace or MCP host control comparable to MSO.

workspace.note: Container consoles, logs, stack editors, and resource views; not a general host files/editor workspace.

hostOps.note: Strong container-platform operations, but host systemd/network/storage administration is outside the core scope.

delivery.note: Docker/Swarm/Kubernetes/Podman resources, stacks, GitOps updates, environment management, and migration/duplication.

observability.note: Container state, logs, and resource inspection; not a Netdata-class observability system.

delegation.note: Access controls are available; advanced RBAC is edition-dependent.

aiControl.note: No native AI/MCP workspace control plane.

workspace.note: Rich monitoring dashboard rather than a files/terminal/editor workspace.

hostOps.note: Observes hosts and services; it is not a general administration shell.

delivery.note: Does not provide general application deployment workflows.

observability.note: Per-second metrics, alerts, anomaly scores, correlation, cross-node analysis, and AI-generated incident insights.

delegation.note: Cloud/team access exists, but identity and remote host access are not its primary comparison axis.

aiControl.note: AI Insights explains telemetry and recommends actions; it does not expose a general host-action MCP surface.

workspace.note: An access layer, not a graphical workspace.

hostOps.note: Carries SSH sessions to the host; administration remains command-line tooling on the target.

observability.note: Connection/audit data is not host observability.

delegation.note: Identity, ACLs, SSH checks, session controls, revocation, and recording integrations are core strengths.

workspace.note: Strong upload/delete/preview/edit file surface, without a complete server workspace.

hostOps.note: No general service, package, network, or storage administration.

delegation.note: File-focused users/scopes, not a complete host privilege model.

workspace.note: Excellent terminal transport, but intentionally only one command/terminal surface.

hostOps.note: Any operations come from the command it exposes, not from structured host controls.

delegation.note: Basic/auth-proxy options and read-only mode, without a product-wide role model.

workspace.note: Friendly personal-cloud dashboard, files, widgets, and apps, but not a developer/operations workspace with full PTY/editor depth.

hostOps.note: Home-server status and storage/app management rather than deep Linux administration.

delivery.note: One-click Docker application ecosystem, not Git/preview-oriented PaaS delivery.

observability.note: Dashboard status/widgets without specialist alerting and RCA depth.

delegation.note: Not positioned around least-privilege team administration.

workspace.note: App-centric home-server dashboard rather than a unified developer/operations workspace.

hostOps.note: General Linux host administration is not the primary product surface.

delivery.note: Curated/custom app stores, preconfigured Compose apps, lifecycle, logs, updates, persistence, and per-app backups.

observability.note: App state/logs, not deep infrastructure observability.

delegation.note: Not positioned as a multi-admin identity/RBAC control plane.
